rounds.text: The market is currently misjudging the momentum of Inland Printers Ltd by focusing on historical averages rather than the clear acceleration in recent performance. While the company has faced past headwinds, the most recent data shows a significant turnaround with net profit growth of 22% year-over-year [E37]. This growth is not a one-off event but part of an accelerating trend [E40] that is currently being ignored by the broader market sentiment [E43]. Furthermore, the company has successfully strengthened its balance sheet by aggressively reducing borrowings from Rs 1.07 Cr to Rs 0.25 Cr [E22], demonstrating a commitment to fiscal discipline [E30]. This financial cleanup is reflected in the market's reaction, with the share price delivering an 84% return over the last year [E12]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with a negative return on equity [E6], [E15], [E41], a high price-to-book valuation [E1], [E31], [E42], and negative operating cash flow [E18], [E19]. Despite these legacy issues, the current trajectory of earnings growth [E39] suggests that the business is in the early stages of a fundamental shift that the current valuation has yet to fully incorporate [E43].

The bull’s reliance on recent profit growth [E37, E38, E40] ignores the reality that the company is fundamentally destroying value, as evidenced by a persistent negative return on equity of -23.1% [E6] and a median ROE of -18% over the last three years [E14]. While the bull highlights debt reduction [E22, E30], this fiscal discipline is overshadowed by the fact that the company generated negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -1.39 Cr in Mar 2026 [E19, E20]. Conceded: the company has reduced borrowings [E22, E30] and achieved an 84% share price return over the last year [E12]. However, this price appreciation has decoupled from performance, as evidenced by the fact that price growth exceeds profit growth by 87% [E28]. Furthermore, the valuation is disconnected from the underlying business quality, with a price-to-book ratio of 24.31x [E1, E31] that is difficult to justify given the company's negative ROCE of -8.8% [E5]. Ultimately, the bull’s "turnaround" narrative is undermined by the company's low promoter holding of 16.94% [E24, E33] and a lack of institutional confidence [E25, E26].
